title: Reading speed, and reading without transliteration

bigIdea.text: Fluent reading means accurate first, then quicker. Every week, read a short passage aloud, count your mistakes and your words per minute, and watch both improve. From now on, read from the Arabic only.

proper.text: Accuracy comes first: a reading counts only if every letter, vowel and length is right. Aim for 98% or more correct words (master mode) before you try to go faster.
Words per minute (wpm) = words read ÷ minutes taken. In this text Al-Ikhlas (112:1–4) has 15 words and Al-Fatiha (1:1–1:7) has 29, so reading Al-Fatiha in 1.5 minutes is about 19 wpm.

provenance.source: Tanzil text: recited-word counts of surahs 1 and 112

proper.text: Measure the same way every time: the same passage, a calm and clear pace, and one counting rule: a word is wrong if any letter, vowel or length in it is wrong.

Transliteration (Arabic written in Latin letters) only helps at the very start. It can't show the Arabic sounds exactly, so read from the Arabic alone from now on. By the end of Stage 1 you read without it.
Speed is not the goal of recitation: the Quran is recited calmly and clearly (tartil). Reading speed only shows that your eyes now recognise words quickly.

extras.text: Keep a simple log: date, passage, accuracy % and words per minute. Comparing week 1 with week 6 shows real progress, even on days that feel slow.

note.text: Al-Ikhlas has 15 words in all (112:1–4): a good first timing passage.

drills.prompt: Timed read: read 112:1–4 aloud at a calm pace while timing yourself, then count any wrong words.
Read 113:1–5 from the Arabic only, without any Latin letters, then check it with Sheikh al-Minshawi.

questions.q: What comes first in fluent reading?
explain: Speed only counts once the reading is accurate.
Melody comes much later and never before correctness.

questions.q: You read 30 words in 2 minutes. What is your speed?
When does a word count as wrong in a speed test?
options: If any letter, vowel or length in it is wrong
Only if you read it twice
explain: A wrong vowel is a mistake too.
Repeating is not the only error.

options: Latin letters can't show Arabic sounds exactly, and your eyes must learn the Arabic
explain: Speed of loading is not the reason.
It isn't forbidden; it is just a crutch.
Tajweed colours are on the Arabic text.

questions.q: What accuracy should you reach before pushing your speed?
explain: Half the words wrong is far too many.
One in four words wrong is still too many.

questions.q: Your speed went up, but your mistakes doubled. What should you do?
options: Slow down until accuracy is back to 98% or more
explain: Measuring is how you notice this.

questions.q: Al-Fatiha has 29 words in this text. You read it in 1 minute 30 seconds. About how many words per minute is that?
explain: That multiplies by 1.5 instead of dividing.
That is too slow for these numbers.

provenance.source: Tanzil text: 29 recited words in surah 1

questions.q: How often should you repeat the speed test?
options: Regularly, for example once a week, on the same passage
explain: Without tests you can't see change.

questions.q: Is reading fast the goal of recitation?
options: No: recite calmly (tartil); speed only shows your eyes recognise words quickly
explain: Calm, clear recitation is the aim there too.
That is not a percentage of anything.
That is the time per word.

questions.q: You read 15 words and 1 is wrong. What is your accuracy?
explain: That would need far more words with one mistake.
That would be about 2 mistakes in 15.

questions.q: Which is a fair way to compare your speed over time?
options: Same passage, same calm pace, same counting rule
Only time the parts you know best

questions.q: By the end of Stage 1, how should you read?
options: From the Arabic text alone, without transliteration
Only with tajweed colours switched on
explain: Listening helps, but you must read.
Colours help, but you read the letters themselves.

remnote: Reading speed == Words per minute = words read ÷ minutes
Reading accuracy == Right words ÷ total words × 100; aim for 98%+ before going faster
When a word counts as wrong == Any wrong letter, vowel or length
Transliteration by the end of Stage 1 == Gone: read from the Arabic only
taskNow: Time yourself reading Al-Ikhlas (112:1–4) aloud at a calm pace, count your wrong words, and write down your accuracy and your words per minute (15 words ÷ your minutes).
